newsitem.title: UK: From the Flightdeck - The Air Cargo Week In Review.
newsitem.headline: From the Flightdeck - The Air Cargo Week In Review.

text.p: This is Reuters look back at the major developments in the air cargo industry in the week January 31 - February 7.
**JANUARY 31**
SEOUL - IATA says North Korea would be ready to open up its airspace for overflights by foreign carriers early this year.
STOCKHOLM - Swedish aircraft maker Saab Aircraft says Slovakian airline Tatra Air ordered two SAAB 2000s.
BRUSSELS - A Commission official says the EC may impose conditions on airlines' rights to airport slots on busy routes in return for allowing them to sell unwanted slots.
* Spokesman Constantin Verros says EC efforts to revise slot allocation rules are not linked to its probes into a series of transatlantic aviation alliances.
LONDON - European transport minister Neil Kinnock says the EC's competition and transport commissioners are involved in talks aimed at resolving the issue of allowing airline slots to be sold.
NEW DELHI - Aviation experts says India needs huge doses of private investment to build vital airport infrastructure and spruce up flight safety.
COPENHAGEN - SAS says it will fight hard to define its dominant position in Scandinavian air traffic, as other carrier invade its home territory.
HONG KONG - The Hong Kong Airport Authority says it awarded a HK$93.6 million contract for traffic control and surveillance systems to General Electric.
* The authority says it awarded a HK$174.7 million contract to Chinese state-owned China State Construction Engineering Corp for works in the territory's new airport.
* The authority says it awarded a HK$13.2 million contract to Advance Specialist Treatment Engineering for epoxy floor finishes in the passenger terminal of the territory's new airport being built.
MOSCOW - Lufthansa says it will begin regular flights between Frankfurt and Perm, in Russia's Ural mountain region via Kazan, the capital of Tatarstan.
PARIS - ADP says New York was the top airport gateway for imports to Charles de Gaulle and Orly airports in 1996.
* ADP says New York was the top export destination from Charles De Gaulle and Orly in 1996.
MUNICH - The airport authority says a second passenger terminal is being built at Munich airport at a cost of up to 1.7 billion marks.
* It says air Cargo flown from Munich rose 17.6 percent to 75,911 tonnes last year. December cargo handled rose 26.8 percent to 7,664 tonnes.
* It adds that the airport broke even for the first time last year and expects to show an overall profit in 1997.
KIEV - Company officials says Boeing and Airbus must wait until March to hear if they have won a tender to help replace state-owned Air Ukraine's fleet.
FRANKFURT - Schenker-Rhenus says it has taken over management of the Scandinavian distribution terminal of German chemicals giant BASF.
ZURICH - Swissair says its partner airlines Austrian Airlines has decided to scrap its flights from Geneva to Washington and instead fly to Zurich.
PARIS - Air France and Alitalia says they have signed a cooperation deal which will take effect on April 1, when Europe's skies will be opened up to full competition.
ROME - BA says it will launch a weekly all-cargo flight from Pisa's Amerigo Vespucci airport on the Tel Aviv-Pisa-London Gatwick route from April 1.
GENEVA - ACI says Memphis, was the world's busiest cargo airport in January-October 1996.
ROME - A new viaduct opened yesterday to complete an elevated road linking Rome-Fiumincino highway and the national and international flight terminals.
BRUSSELS - Air Hong Kong air is increasing its rates ex-Europe from March.
AMSTERDAM - Amsterdam's air cargo forwarders and GSA's are again calling for a withdrawal of the fuel surcharge following the latest round of airline rates increases.
NEW YORK - Kiwi International Air Lines says it sued ValuJet alleging the discount carrier did not pay Kiwi for charter services provided in December.
ST.LOUIS - McDonnell Douglas says it named Walter Orlowski as president of Douglas Aircraft Co., its commercial aircraft unit in Long Beach, California.
WASHINGTON - Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth says the Airport Trust Fund may be depleted "much earlier" than originally projected.
**FEBRUARY 1**
SANAA - An airline official says Yemen's national carrier Yemen Airways will start an air cargo service for the first time in April.
BEIRUT - Saudi Arabian Airlines says it resumed flights to Beirut after a halt of nearly 15 years due to Lebanon's 1975-1990 civil war.
AMSTERDAM - EU transport ministers urged the EC to push ahead with institutionalising air transport safety during the final day of an informal transport council in Amsterdam.
WASHINGTON - The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency says it has put off until late summer implementation of controversial tougher clean air standards to allow more time for public comment.
**FEBRUARY 2**

PARIS - Les Echos says Alcatel Alsthom has found two French partners in state-owned Aerospatiale and Dassault to prepare a bid for state-controller electronics firm Thomson-CSF and is waiting to hear the government's terms for privatisation of the latter.
**FEBRUARY 3**

TAIPEI - Airport officials says cargo handlers at Taiwan's main airport began refusing to work overtime of off-hours, saying that authorities has ignored their interests in privatising a state-run cargo centre.
JOHANNESBURG - SAA says it was buying two additional Boeing 747-400s powered by Rolls-Royce engines, ending months of uncertainty about the order.
LONDON - A UK government spokesman says crucial talks between UK and U.S. officials on negotiating a new 'open skies' agreement due to a senior negotiator falling ill.
LONDON - UK airport group BAA says it had decided to cut the stake in its bid group for Australian airports to 29 percent from 49 percent.
